title: Nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations in two-photon-driven nonlinear quantum optical systems
authors: Y. T. Chen, Y. W. Lu, J. C. Lu, C. Wang
abstract: Understanding nonequilibrium transport and fluctuations driven by nonclassical light in nonlinear quantum optical systems is challenging. Here, we formulate a driven quantum master equation in the rotating frame combined with full counting statistics, retaining the drive-induced frequency shifts in the system-reservoir interactions and providing a unified description of drive-assisted incoherent transitions based on the rotated system dressed-basis. Applied to a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model, the approach reveals pronounced multiphoton-resonant enhancement of the drive input energy current, with significant high peaks under two-photon driving compared to the single-photon case. The two-photon resonance relations are analytically obtained. Resonance structure in the nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model nonlinearly relies on qubit-photon couplings, with additional dressed-state branches. A low-energy-state approximation attributes the resonant current enhancement to dressed-state hybridization and efficient activation of incoherent energy exchange processes. Beyond the average current, two-photon-driving induced energy exchange picture near resonance also substantially modifies the second-order current fluctuation and higher-order current cumulant, while increasing the time-normalized signal-to-noise ratio. Adding two-photon loss introduces extra incoherent photon-pair exchange pathways and further reshapes the current and its fluctuations. We hope these results may deepen interpretation of photon driving and quantum dissipation cooperatively governing nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a comprehensive framework using Full Counting Statistics to analyze energy transport and fluctuations in nonlinear quantum optical systems driven by two-photon light. It demonstrates that two-photon resonance leads to enhanced energy currents and improved signal-to-noise ratios compared to single-photon driving. The methodology is crucial for interpreting quantum dissipation effects in advanced quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex challenge of understanding nonequilibrium energy transport and fluctuations when driven by nonclassical light in nonlinear quantum optical systems.
main_result: The study reveals that two-photon driving causes a pronounced, resonant enhancement of the energy current, significantly boosting the signal-to-noise ratio compared to single-photon driving.
method: The authors employ a driven quantum master equation framework combined with the rigorous formalism of Full Counting Statistics (FCS) to calculate current cumulants.
model_or_system: The model applies to quantum optical systems, specifically analyzing a Kerr resonator and a nonlinear Jaynes-Cummings model coupled to bosonic reservoirs. The dynamics are described by a driven quantum master equation formulated in the rotating frame.
key_observables: Energy current (average current), second-order current fluctuation, and higher-order current cumulants.
important_parameters: Two-photon driving strength, resonance conditions, and reservoir temperatures ($T_l, T_r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Born-Markov approximation and utilizes low-energy-state approximations for simplifying the current calculations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 provides a schematic overview of the nonequilibrium quantum optical system setup, showing the cavity coupled to reservoirs.
paper_structure: The paper builds from formulating the driven quantum master equation to applying Full Counting Statistics. It then analyzes the resulting current and fluctuation equations for specific models (Kerr/Jaynes-Cummings), deriving resonance conditions and interpreting the physical origin of the current enhancement via dressed-state hybridization.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides advanced theoretical tools (FCS, driven master equations) to quantify energy flow and noise in driven, dissipative quantum light-matter interactions.
